lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.p450GroundEnergyProgram
lean.annotation: `p450GroundEnergyProgram` takes the system and ancilla register placements. The walk length and 16-qubit phase register are fixed by the solution. The inverse QFT produces the outcome distribution from the accumulated phases without a classical energy input.

lean.annotation: `Pi.single 0 1` is the zero ancilla ket. The Lean sum uses full ancilla outcomes $a$. The decoder uses only the phase bits obtained by `extractIndex`. Summing the probabilities of outcomes with the same phase index $y$ gives the $p(y\mid\psi)$ in Eq. (20).

lean.name: QuantumComputationSpecs.Algorithms.P450GroundEnergy.Solution.SevenGearWalk333.fast7gUnitProg
lean.annotation: The run starts with zeroed ancillas and prepares the phase-gradient resource internally; it does not assume an external gradient state. The ideal 11-wire fine gradient uses phase spacing 2π/2¹⁴, so plain addition modulo 2¹¹ leaves a wrap-dependent phase; the signed phase step accounts for it.

lean.name: RealizesUnitaryFromBasisOutcomesAndZeroWorkspace
lean.annotation: The restriction to zero ancillas applies to the input. The final observable $M$ can act on the full output, including the phase register. Applying the precondition inequality to $M$ and its complement gives equality of expectations on the restricted input subspace.

lean.annotation: `IsEigen` requires $H\psi=E\psi$ and $P_{63}\psi=\psi$. It also requires a nonzero vector, since the zero vector would qualify for every real eigenvalue and make the cutoff impossible. For the eigenvector used as input, the predicate separately requires norm one.

statements.markdown: we do not count this overhead
statements.note: With independent fresh trials and ideal phase estimation, ground-eigenspace weight `p > 0` gives an average of `1/p` preparations and runs to sample that component—ten when `p = 0.1`. The manuscript excludes trial-state preparation and this repetition overhead from its one-run estimate, which includes the circuit’s own ancilla preparation; identifying ground-state outcomes at finite precision needs a separate argument.
